QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_53

question.text: The score-card approach in start-up valuation:

answer.text: Awards additional valuation to start-ups with stronger qualitative attributes such as team, governance, disclosure standards and lower non-compliance, where a higher score can mean better valuation

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 247, 249-250), the workbook recognises that start-up valuations may be adjusted to reflect qualitative attributes through a score card, where a higher score can translate into better valuation. Stronger team, governance, disclosure standards and lower non-compliance are the kinds of qualitative attributes that can lift the score. The Trap: The score-card concept is not DCF-only, does not zero-value start-ups, and is not restricted to post-revenue companies. It is a qualitative overlay on early-stage valuations. Note: Distributors should remember that score-card adjustments are qualitative and judgement-driven, so investors should examine the underlying scoring assumptions rather than the final number alone.
